title: std::conditional_t Type Selection
prompt: Implement `Storage<T>` whose `value_type` is `T` for small types (<= 8 bytes) but `std::shared_ptr<T>` for large ones — via `std::conditional_t` — plus `biggest(a, b)` returning the larger by reference using `std::conditional_t` on a comparison trait is overkill; just use std::conditional_t<std::is_integral_v<T>, int, double> fallback semantics in `numberKind<T>()`.

tests.name: large types store via shared_ptr
tests.code:
struct Big { char pad[64]; };
static_assert(std::is_same_v<Storage<Big>::value_type, std::shared_ptr<Big>>, "big goes indirect");
tests.hint: Same conditional — sizeof(Big) is 64, so the shared_ptr branch selects.

tests.name: Scalar alias switches on integrality
tests.code:
static_assert(std::is_same_v<Scalar<int>, long long>, "integral -> long long");
static_assert(std::is_same_v<Scalar<double>, double>, "floating -> double");
tests.hint: template <class T> using Scalar = std::conditional_t<std::is_integral_v<T>, long long, double>;
